sourceMetadata.title: 3D Reference Organ for Brain, Female
sourceMetadata.description:
This reference organ, Brain-female (https://humanatlas.io/3d-reference-library) was created using data from the Allen
brain reference atlas (Ding et al. 2016). The 141 anatomical structures were mirrored to arrive at a whole human brain
(as intended) and resized to fit the Visible Human Male and Female bodies (Spitzer et al. 1996; Ackerman 1998; Spitzer
and Whitlock 2002). In version v1.3, an update in licensing occurred; this brain model is now licensed under Creative
Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0). Ding et al. 2016 was used to inform the creation of this model.

**Bibliography:**

* Ackerman, Michael J. 1998. “The Visible Human Project.” *Proceedings of the IEEE* 86 (3): 504–11. https://doi.org/10.1109/5.662875.
* Ding, Song-Lin, Joshua J. Royall, Susan M. Sunkin, Lydia Ng, Benjamin A.C. Facer, Phil Lesnar, Angie Guillozet-Bongaarts, et al. 2016. “Comprehensive Cellular-Resolution Atlas of the Adult Human Brain.” *Journal of Comparative Neurology* 524 (16): 3127–3481.
* Spitzer, Victor M., and David G. Whitlock. 2002. “The Visible Human Dataset: The Anatomical Platform for Human Simulation.” *The Anatomical Record* 253 (2): 49–57. https://doi.org/10.1002/(SICI)1097-0185(199804)253:2<49::AID-AR8>3.0.CO;2-9.

sourceMetadata.title: 3D Reference Organ for Eye, Female, Left
sourceMetadata.description:
This reference organ, Left-eye-female (https://humanatlas.io/3d-reference-library) was created using data from the
Visible Human Dataset, provided by the National Library of Medicine (Spitzer and Whitlock 2002). The long posterior
ciliary artery was added, as well as a more detailed iris. The position of the optic nerve also moved, and made twice
as thick. The muscle thickness was decreased and the position of the muscles was shifted. The levator palpebrae
superioris muscle was removed as it was not deemed necessary to the eye model. The inferior oblique muscle was rotated
more parallel to the plane of the cornea.

**Bibliography:**

* Spitzer, Victor M., and David G. Whitlock. 2002. “The Visible Human Dataset: The Anatomical Platform for Human Simulation.” *The Anatomical Record* 253 (2): 49–57. https://doi.org/10.1002/(SICI)1097-0185(199804)253:2<49::AID-AR8>3.0.CO;2-9.

This reference organ, Left-eye-male (https://humanatlas.io/3d-reference-library) was created using data from the
Visible Human Male, provided by the National Library of Medicine (Spitzer et al. 1996; Ackerman 1998). In version
v1.3, the long posterior ciliary artery was added, as well as a more detailed iris. The position of the optic nerve
also moved, and was made twice as thick. The muscle thickness was decreased and the position of the muscles was
shifted. The levator palpebrae superioris muscle was removed as it was not deemed necessary to the eye model. The
inferior oblique muscle was rotated more parallel to the plane of the cornea.

**Bibliography:**

* Ackerman, Michael J. 1998. “The Visible Human Project.” *Proceedings of the IEEE* 86 (3): 504–11. https://doi.org/10.1109/5.662875.
* Spitzer, V., M. J. Ackerman, A. L. Scherzinger, and D. Whitlock. 1996. “The Visible Human Male: A Technical Report.” *Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association* 3 (2): 118–30. https://doi.org/10.1136/jamia.1996.96236280.

sourceMetadata.title: 3D Reference Organ for Placenta, Full Term, Female
sourceMetadata.description:
This reference organ, Placenta-full-term-female (https://humanatlas.io/3d-reference-library) was created using a
sculpted model of the placenta, partly informed by MRI data from the Department of Obstetrics, Gynecology, and
Reproductive Sciences, Division of Maternal-Fetal Medicine at UC San Diego Health. *Human Microscopic Anatomy* (Krstić
1991) and Mannelli et al. 2015 were consulted.

**Bibliography:**

* Krstić, Radivoj V. 1991. *Human Microscopic Anatomy*. Berlin, Heidelberg: Springer. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-662-02676-2.
* Mannelli, Chiara, Francesca Ietta, Anna Maria Avanzati, Dariusz Skarzynski, and Luana Paulesu. 2015. “Biological Tools to Study the Effects of Environmental Contaminants at the Feto–Maternal Interface.” *Dose-Response* 13 (4): 1559325815611902. https://doi.org/10.1177/1559325815611902.
sourceMetadata.citation: Schlehlein, Heidi. 2024. "3D Reference Organ for Placenta, Full Term, Female v1.1." https://doi.org/10.48539/HBM593.ZRJH.644. Accessed on June 15, 2024.

sourceMetadata.title: 3D Reference Organ for Skin, Female
sourceMetadata.description:
This reference organ, Skin-female (https://humanatlas.io/3d-reference-library) was created using data from the Visible
Human Dataset, provided by the National Library of Medicine (Spitzer and Whitlock 2002). In version v1.3, the torso of
the skin model was moved up from previous editions to incorporate the clavicles and other anatomy for the breast. It
was also adjusted to add space for the triceps surae and the ankle bones for the eventual addition of the triceps
surae muscles and landmark organs. In v2.3, the head was adjusted to be more like the original skin of the Visible
Human Female, to make space for the mouth 3D object and landmarks.

**Bibliography:**

* Spitzer, Victor M., and David G. Whitlock. 2002. “The Visible Human Dataset: The Anatomical Platform for Human Simulation.” *The Anatomical Record* 253 (2): 49–57. https://doi.org/10.1002/(SICI)1097-0185(199804)253:2<49::AID-AR8>3.0.CO;2-9.

sourceMetadata.title: 3D Reference Organ for Small Intestine, Female
sourceMetadata.description:
This reference organ, Small-intestine-female (https://humanatlas.io/3d-reference-library) was created using data from
the Visible Human Dataset, provided by the National Library of Medicine (Spitzer and Whitlock 2002). The small
intestines have been updated to include a measurement system. A centerline was made in the center of the intestines,
and markers placed along the centerline. The teal discs measure 5 cm along the intestines, the green dashes measure 1
cm. The yellow disc marks the jejunoileal junction. The Visible Human Female small intestine total length is 200 cm.

**Bibliography:**

* Spitzer, Victor M., and David G. Whitlock. 2002. “The Visible Human Dataset: The Anatomical Platform for Human Simulation.” *The Anatomical Record* 253 (2): 49–57. https://doi.org/10.1002/(SICI)1097-0185(199804)253:2<49::AID-AR8>3.0.CO;2-9.

sourceMetadata.title: 3D Reference Organ for Small Intestine, Male
sourceMetadata.description:
This reference organ, Small-intestine-male (https://humanatlas.io/3d-reference-library) was created using data from
the Visible Human Male, provided by the National Library of Medicine (Spitzer et al. 1996; Ackerman 1998). The small
intestines have been updated to include a measurement system. A centerline was made in the center of the intestines,
and markers were placed along the centerline. The teal discs measure 5 cm along the intestines, the green dashes
measure 1 cm, and the yellow disc marks the jejunoileal junction. The Visible Human Male small intestine total length
is 285 cm.

**Bibliography:**

* Ackerman, Michael J. 1998. “The Visible Human Project.” *Proceedings of the IEEE* 86 (3): 504–11. https://doi.org/10.1109/5.662875.
* Spitzer, V., M. J. Ackerman, A. L. Scherzinger, and D. Whitlock. 1996. “The Visible Human Male: A Technical Report.” *Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association* 3 (2): 118–30. https://doi.org/10.1136/jamia.1996.96236280.
